## TL;DR

Completed the requested rendered contrast QA pass from the task worktree. Built the app artifacts required by the audit and ran `bun run contrast:audit`, which uses headless WebKit. The configured matrix covered 16 theme scopes and 14 screen states. It examined 15,254 visible text runs and reported no text below the WCAG contrast floor. No UI changes or regression tests were justified by the evidence. Added the QA record at `docs/qa/2026-11-theme-contrast-qa.md`.

## Work and rationale

I first confirmed the active directory was the assigned feature worktree and that it began clean. I read the task file from that worktree and inspected the audit implementation and browser tests to understand what the command actually does. The task explicitly forbids changes to `repoos.toml`, and I left it untouched.

The configured matrix contains classic dark and light plus Clear, Gen Z, Jelly, Gruvbox, Catppuccin, Hypercolor, and Solarized, each in both modes. The rendered audit builds a fixture application, launches WebKit headlessly, and drives a list of screen preparations before changing the root theme scope and probing computed styles. It applies the same scope to the live page before each probe and retries failed probes to avoid a transient theme-flip frame being mistaken for a real problem. This meant the appropriate first action was to run the existing browser-based audit rather than infer contrast from source token values alone.

The first command attempt could not run because the task worktree did not contain the compiled `dist/commands/ui-contrast-audit.js` artifact. This is expected in a fresh worktree because `dist/` is ignored and should not be committed. I ran `bun run build` in the task worktree, which completed successfully, then reran `bun run contrast:audit`.

The audit result was a pass: 16 theme scope(s) × 14 screen state(s), 15,254 visible text runs examined, 320 exempted runs, 64 disabled-component runs skipped, zero invisible runs skipped, and 7,931 text runs judged against the worst stop of a gradient. It found no text below the WCAG floor in any theme scope. The separate `background-clip: text` category had 14 unchecked runs from the gradient logo. This is a limitation of the text-run probe, not a reported contrast failure; I recorded it explicitly so the QA result does not overclaim coverage. The existing collapsed board label/count exemption also remains documented in the project’s existing contrast triage record.

Because this pass produced no reproducible failing selector or state, I did not modify theme tokens, add a local color override, or create a test that would assert an invented regression. The result and reproduction steps are recorded in the requested QA document. The audit command itself and all theme configuration remain unchanged.

## Approaches tried

I checked the audit command and its browser-level tests first to establish whether it was using a real browser engine, what theme scopes it consumed, and how it represented unavailable browser support. The script exposed that it requires compiled command output, so an initial run stopped with a specific missing-artifact message. I then built with the repository’s Bun build command and reran the audit. This is a normal source-to-dist workflow for this worktree; `dist/` is generated and ignored.

I used the rendered audit rather than visual browser inspection because the acceptance criterion requires headless Playwright and the repository’s probe measures actual rendered text against its background, including gradient stops. I did not use a headed browser, open any URL, or take focus from the user. I also did not widen the task into source-only color searches: the rendered pass covered the declared pages and dialog states in all configured themes, and there were no failure rows to guide targeted source investigation.

## Challenges and blockers

The only setup issue was the absent ignored build output. The first audit attempt failed before rendering; the build resolved it, and the subsequent audit completed normally. There were no Playwright availability errors, server startup errors, unavailable screen states, or contrast failures.

The audit reports gradient-clipped logo text as unchecked rather than assigning it a contrast result. This is a known boundary of the current probe. The run still has useful rendered coverage for ordinary text, gradient-backed text judged at the worst gradient stop, and the registered dialogs and screen fixtures. I reported the unchecked count rather than treating it as a pass or failure. No human device or account was needed for this acceptance criterion.

## Key learnings

A fresh task worktree may not have `dist/`; building before using the compiled contrast command is sufficient, and generated output must stay out of the branch. The current audit’s theme matrix is broad: eight UI theme families, both modes, and 14 prepared screen states. Its output distinguishes visible text it judged, configured exemptions, disabled or invisible content, gradient worst-stop judgments, and text it cannot judge due to `background-clip: text`. Preserving those categories in the QA record makes the passing result auditable without suggesting every rendered pixel was evaluated.

For this pass, the evidence supports documenting a clean result rather than making speculative token edits. A future audit failure should be followed from its selector and theme scope into the component’s semantic token use, then fixed with a token-based change and a regression test for the demonstrated defect.
